answer: Agents periodically broadcast a signed “orchard” ledger of their recent tasks, each entry stamped with a unique cryptographic signal tied to their hardware fingerprint; a random jury of peers pulls a river‑wide sample of these entries and runs spot‑check audits, rejecting any ledger that fails consistency. Because each audit requires the attacker to forge distinct hardware fingerprints and duplicate the signal for dozens of unrelated agents, the cost scales linearly with the number of fake identities, quickly outweighing any benefit.
